+Ve regurge

  • Reflux of pus or tears from the puncta in case of obstruction of the naso-lacrimal duct. (In Chronic dacrocystitis)

  • This is a definite proof of obstruction.

-Ve regurge

  • no reflux with patent lacrimal passages.

Chronic dacryocystitis

  • Test: Regurgitation Test ( showing purulent discharge at Rt. picture)

  • Management: *

    • - Dacryocystorhinostomy .

    • - Dacryocystectomy is only indicated in certain cases

    • - Treatment of the cause of obstruction

Congenital nasolacrimal duct obstruction

Differentiate it from conjunctivitis.

  • No red eye + there is watery discharge at the other eye.

Management?

  • In the first 9-12 months of age ➝ 

  • 1-Medical treatment in the form of topical antibiotics and digital massage (by the mother using her little finger) on the sac then in a downward direction the nose, to push the secretions and open Hasner's valve.

  • 2-If there is no improvement by medical treatment after the age of 1 year ➝ Probing is indicated (it could be repeated once more)

  • -If the second probing fails too ➝ silastic intubation of the lacrimal passages is performed.

  • -If intubation fails ➝ Dacryosyctorhinostomy is indicated.

Acute orbital cellulitis

Manifestation

  • Dystopia ( مهم تذكرها عشان لو مجبش صورة ال CT كحاجة تفرق عن ال preseptal )

  • Severe eyelid edema and redness + Chemosis

  • Proptosis

  • Opacifications posterior to orbital septum

  • Honeycomb Appearance + Enlargement of extraocular muscles.

Management

  • Hospitalization: is necessary in orbital cellulitis only for close follow-up:

    1. Topical and systemic parenteral broad spectrum antibiotics.

    2. Hot foments.

  • N.B: If abscess is formed, it should be drained

Acute dacryocystitis

  • Management : Draining under cover of antibiotics
